title: Execution When a Predicate Holds
statement: Let $W,F,\mathrm{pos},\mathrm{size},l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{code}$ be a program for a word RAM with $W$-bit words, let $m$ be its initial memory, and let $p$ be a proposition. Suppose there exist a memory $m'$ and a number $n\le\mathrm{size}$ such that $m'$ agrees with $m$ at every address outside the scratch set, and the program runs for $n$ steps from program position $\mathrm{pos}$ and memory $m'$ whenever $p$ holds, reaching position $\mathrm{pos}+\mathrm{size}$. If $p$ holds, then there exist such an $m'$ and $n\le\mathrm{size}$, with the same agreement outside the scratch set, for which the program runs from position $\mathrm{pos}$ and memory $m$ for $n$ steps to position $\mathrm{pos}+\mathrm{size}$. Here the scratch set consists of addresses $-21,-15,-17,-19,-13$ and addresses $-(23+4j)$ for integers $j$ with $0\le j\le 2F$.
